title: Graph Beta: authenticated current-graph query
description: Objective: make the existing graph.get query reachable through the production daemon HTTP/MCP path without copying projection logic. Deliverable: a bounded query handler/port branch that authenticates the session, derives the project/principal from the authenticated request context, calls task-dd4ffa0c40834c59892f957fbf61fb23's public durable current-active reader, and returns its immutable snapshot plus revision/epoch/content provenance. Hard dependency: task-dd4ffa0c40834c59892f957fbf61fb23 with the GraphRevisionContent authority decision resolved. NOT in scope: graph mutations, registry command decisions, new runtime kinds, Foundation attempt dispatch or UI. Consumer/final hardening: task-efc2ef6330074b4d9893809f7425c95f. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test.
definitionOfDone: The frozen graph.get query kind is handled by the real production HTTP/MCP authentication and query dispatch path; project and principal come from the authenticated context and no payload/query field can select a different project or active revision.

The handler calls task-dd4ffa0c40834c59892f957fbf61fb23's public reader and returns the exact deeply frozen current snapshot, revision identity, graphEpoch, full graphContentHash provenance and separately named structural snapshot identity without equating the two.

No active graph, malformed/noncanonical history, multiple active revisions, receipt/decision mismatch or unreadable store state preserves the reader's exact stable code/layer and returns UNKNOWN/no snapshot authority.

Real Authenticator + SqliteEventStore tests cover unauthenticated/capability/project spoofing before reader invocation, every reader refusal with exact code/layer, nonzero hostile cases, and one accepted production event-to-MCP control; query reads leave event/decision counts unchanged.
Daemon typecheck and test gates execute with nonzero Test Files/Tests counts, public runtime bridges load under plain Node, and production files remain focused under the per-file cap.
taskRails: Consume the durable projection; do not copy its fold or trust scanned event payloads directly.
Use only existing graph.get vocabulary and real HTTP/MCP authentication; no new schema/kind, no command-decision write and no caller-selected authority.
Wait for dec-64b2391cb80f4c0cbb6e88353017cc65; never label scheduler graphIdentity as graphContentHash. TDD and explicit-path discipline apply.

The unequated pair is real at the reader, from two DIFFERENT sources — this is what makes the anti-equation test meaningful rather than tautological. `ActiveGraphAccepted` (:73-84) declares `graphContentHash: string` and `snapshotIdentity: string` as separate fields, and the return at :205-218 fills them from different places: `graphContentHash: current.state.graphContentHash` (the revision STATE's content provenance, covering all seven design-197 fields) and `snapshotIdentity: body.snapshotIdentity` (the BODY RECORD's structure-only value, graph-body-record.ts:74, :189). implementationPlan.description:
TESTS FIRST. Create apps/daemon/src/planning/graph-query.test.ts over a REAL `Authenticator` and a REAL file-backed `SqliteEventStore` (`openForProject`), closed in a `finally` on every exit path.
Seed one ACTIVE graph revision through the production writer path that `active-graph-projection.test.ts` already uses — read that file and reuse its seeding shape rather than hand-writing revision events. The reader's claims are about durable rows the graph writer produced; a hand-built event would make every assertion a statement about the fixture.
Write RED, the accepted control first: an authenticated `graph.get` returns the exact snapshot the reader returned, with `revisionId`, `graphEpoch`, `graphContentHash` and `snapshotIdentity` all present as SEPARATE fields.
THE ANTI-EQUATION ASSERTION, which is this task's defining test: assert `answer.graphContentHash !== answer.snapshotIdentity` for a seeded revision whose two values genuinely differ, AND assert each equals the corresponding field of the reader's own `ActiveGraphAccepted` result. Comparing against the reader's output rather than against hand-written hex is what keeps the assertion attached to production; a test that hard-codes both operands is a tautology.
Also assert up front that raw event and command-decision counts are unchanged across every query — DoD 4 requires it, and it is measured from the store, never inferred from the return value.
Confirm the suite fails because the handler does not exist, not because the harness is wrong.

Land the shared handler: apps/daemon/src/planning/graph-query.ts plus its EXACT one-line LF bridge `export * from "./graph-query.ts";`.
FOLLOW THE AFFORDANCE PRECEDENT, which is the closest analog already in the tree — `serveAffordances` (http-listener.ts:158-180) authenticates, checks availability, reads the request, and refuses when the request names a project other than `options.affordances.boundProjectId`. Mirror that shape exactly rather than inventing a second one.
Declare a NARROW READ-ONLY PORT here so neither transport can reach a writer:
```
export interface GraphQueryPort {
  readonly boundProjectId: string;
  readCurrentActiveGraph(projectId: string): ActiveGraphResult;
}
```
One reader plus the bound project, and no commit method — "this query writes nothing" becomes a property of the type rather than a rule to remember.
`answerGraphQuery({authenticator, port, credential, protocolVersion, body})`:
1. `authenticateHttpRequest(authenticator, credential, protocolVersion)` — the SAME production function both transports already use, so the guard order (authenticate -> compatibility) is shared rather than re-implemented. A refusal is returned with its own stage, code and httpStatus verbatim.
2. Require the capability the affordance/read surface requires; use an EXISTING capability constant from the registry's vocabulary rather than minting one. Record which you chose and why in the module header.
3. PROJECT COMES FROM THE PRINCIPAL: `principal.projectId`, cross-checked against `port.boundProjectId`. If the request body names a project at all, it must equal both or refuse — DoD 1 requires that no payload or query field can select a different project, and the affordance path already models the check.
4. Call `port.readCurrentActiveGraph(principal.projectId)`.
5. On refusal, return the reader's `code`, `layer`, `sourceCode` and `sourceLayer` VERBATIM. That struct exists precisely so a caller can tell which layer answered; flattening it would make ACTIVE_GRAPH_ABSENT indistinguishable from a body-record failure.
6. On success, return a deeply frozen answer carrying the snapshot, revisionId, graphEpoch, planHash, provenance, `graphContentHash` and `snapshotIdentity` — the last two under those two distinct names, never merged, never cross-assigned.

COMPOSE THE PORT where the daemon's other read surfaces are composed — apps/daemon/src/daemon-store-dependencies.ts builds the provider and apps/daemon/src/daemon-entry.ts threads options to the listener; measure which one owns the affordance/subscription wiring and follow it exactly rather than adding a third composition site.
The port is constructed from the daemon's already-open store and its already-known project id (`createDaemonCommandPorts` takes `projectId` as a server option, and the affordance port already carries a `boundProjectId`). Both are SERVER facts; neither may be read from a request.
Thread it as an OPTIONAL field on the listener options and the MCP config, exactly as `affordances` and `subscriptions` already are. Optional is deliberate and matches the precedent: when the port is absent the transports refuse with an availability code (`serveAffordances` refuses `LISTENER_AFFORDANCES_UNAVAILABLE` when its port is undefined) rather than crashing, so a daemon composed without graph support answers a stable refusal instead of a stack trace.
Do not widen `CommandAdapterDeps` to carry the store: it is `{authenticator, decisions, registry}` and is shared with the command path, which has no business reaching a projection reader.

SERVE IT OVER HTTP. In apps/daemon/src/http/http-listener.ts add a `GRAPH_GET_PATH = "/graph/get"` constant beside the other four route constants (:67-70), add it to the known-route guard at :225-226 so it does not fall through to `LISTENER_ROUTE_UNKNOWN`, add the dispatch arm at :246-249, and add a `serveGraphQuery` that delegates to step 3's `answerGraphQuery` and replies.
Keep the arm THIN: authentication, project derivation and the reader call all live in the shared handler, so this function only adapts request to answer. A second copy of the auth sequence here is exactly the divergence that lets one transport's guard order drift from the other's.
Always reply 200 with the frame carrying its own outcome/code/layer for a READER refusal, matching `serveEventPage`'s documented rule at :126-128 — "the frame IS the answer and carries its own outcome, code and layer. Minting an HTTP status per frame would be the translation table the seam is forbidden to hold." An AUTHENTICATION refusal keeps `access.httpStatus`, as every other route does.
MEASURE `wc -l` AFTER: this file is 304 physical lines and the cap is split-before-400. If the route pushes it near the bound, extract the read routes into a focused sibling module with its own exact one-line LF bridge rather than exceeding it, and record the measured count as the forcing evidence.

SERVE IT OVER MCP — and note the measured asymmetry this step closes.
`dispatchCommandBytes(bytes, context?: HttpDispatchContext)` in apps/daemon/src/mcp-dispatch-port.ts takes a credential-bearing context, but `dispatchQueryBytes(bytes)` (:72) takes NONE, so no principal — and therefore no project — is reachable inside the query path today. `work.get_context` and `events.read` do not need one; `graph.get` does, because DoD 1 requires the project to come from the authenticated context.
The fix is contract-compatible and needs no @moe/mcp change: `StdioDispatchPort` declares `dispatchQueryBytes(bytes: Uint8Array): Uint8Array`, and an implementation may take an ADDITIONAL optional parameter — which is exactly how `dispatchCommandBytes` already carries its context in this same file. Add `context?: HttpDispatchContext` to the query implementation and resolve the credential as the command path does: `context?.credential ?? config.fallbackCredential ?? null` (the config comment states stdio has one identity per process while HTTP always supplies its authenticated bearer).
Add the `graph.get` branch before the `events.read` fallthrough at :89, delegating to `answerGraphQuery` with the resolved credential and `WIRE_PROTOCOL_VERSION`. When the graph port is absent, return the existing `queryRefusal()` rather than a new shape.
Do NOT re-authenticate with a second code path: the port already calls `authenticatorOf(config.deps).authenticate(credential)` at :53 for its `authenticate` method, and the shared handler performs the seam's own authenticate/compatibility sequence. One sequence, reached from both transports.

THE AUTHENTICATION AND SPOOFING MATRIX — DoD 4, and every case must prove the refusal happened BEFORE the reader ran.
Drive each through BOTH transports, asserting the exact code, the exact stage/layer, and — the part a return-value assertion cannot see — that `readCurrentActiveGraph` was never invoked. Wrap the port in a counting decorator for these cases so "refused before reader invocation" is measured rather than assumed; a handler that read first and refused afterwards would leak the existence and shape of another project's graph while still returning a refusal.
- UNAUTHENTICATED: absent credential, and separately a rejected credential -> the authenticator's own refusal with its `httpStatus` and AUTHENTICATE stage preserved.
- WRONG PROTOCOL VERSION -> the COMPATIBILITY stage refusal, distinct from the auth one.
- CAPABILITY DENIED: a principal authenticated for the project but lacking the required capability.
- PROJECT SPOOFING, the case DoD 1 names: a body naming a project OTHER than `principal.projectId`, and separately one naming a project other than `port.boundProjectId`. Both refuse, and neither reaches the reader. This is the assertion that proves no caller-selected authority exists.
- GENERATED HOSTILE SWEEP over the query body: non-object, array, `__proto__`, accessor-bearing field, unlisted extra field, non-NFC project string, oversized string. Assert `cases.length > 0` BEFORE asserting outcomes — a sweep that silently generates zero cases passes while testing nothing — and assert each refuses rather than throwing. A crash is not a refusal.

THE READER REFUSAL PASS-THROUGH — DoD 3. Every one of the reader's own refusals must arrive at the caller with its code, layer, sourceCode and sourceLayer intact, and with NO snapshot and no authority.
Seed each state and assert the exact quadruple:
- NO ACTIVE GRAPH -> `ACTIVE_GRAPH_ABSENT`, layer `ACTIVE_GRAPH_PROJECTION`, sourceLayer null.
- MULTIPLE ACTIVE REVISIONS -> `ACTIVE_GRAPH_SPLIT_BRAIN`. Seed two genuinely active revisions; this is the arm that must never be silently resolved by picking one.
- BODY UNAVAILABLE -> `ACTIVE_GRAPH_BODY_UNAVAILABLE` with sourceLayer `GRAPH_BODY_RECORD` and the body record's OWN `sourceCode` — assert the source fields, not just the outer code, because that pair is the only thing distinguishing a missing body from a corrupt one.
- MALFORMED / NONCANONICAL HISTORY -> the core replay's own `GraphRevisionReplayCode`, which the reader's contract comment says is deliberately NOT merged into this module's three codes so a caller can tell them apart by prefix. Assert the replay code verbatim; a test asserting only "refused" would stay green if the two vocabularies merged.
- UNREADABLE STORE -> the refusal, not a thrown error.
In every case assert the answer carries no snapshot, no revisionId, no graphContentHash and no snapshotIdentity. An UNKNOWN that still leaks a partial identity is authority granted by accident.

THE PRODUCTION EVENT-TO-MCP CONTROL — DoD 4's accepted control, end to end and not stubbed.
Seed an ACTIVE graph revision through the production writer, then issue a real `graph.get` query envelope as BYTES through `dispatchQueryBytes` with an authenticated credential, decode the returned bytes, and assert the snapshot equals the one `readCurrentActiveGraph` returns for the same store and project.
WHY BYTES AND NOT A DIRECT CALL: the MCP path JSON-encodes through `bytesOf`, and a snapshot that is deeply frozen in process can still lose or reorder structure across that boundary. Comparing the decoded bytes against the reader's own output is what proves the transport is faithful rather than merely responsive — the same reasoning `tests/integration/control-room/control-room-transport.test.ts` documents for its payload equality.
Assert `graphContentHash` and `snapshotIdentity` both survive the round trip as distinct fields with distinct values. A JSON boundary is exactly where two same-shaped hex strings could be collapsed by a careless projection, and this is the last place to catch it.
Also run the identical query twice and assert byte-identical answers, and that event and decision counts are unchanged across both.

MUTATION DRILLS against the production surface. Run each, record the exact test name that reddened, restore, and confirm restored bytes hash-match the original — git status alone is unreliable in this shared worktree, where a foreign hook commit can swallow a drill.
1. THE DECOY DRILL, and it is the one this task exists to prevent: in the handler, return `snapshotIdentity` as the value of `graphContentHash` (or assign one from the other). The anti-equation test must redden. If it does not, the suite is not actually distinguishing the two values and the task has landed green and wrong — exactly the failure the prior architect's handoff predicted.
2. Take `projectId` from the request body instead of `principal.projectId`. The project-spoofing test must redden AND the counting decorator must show the reader was invoked.
3. Delete the `boundProjectId` cross-check. The second spoofing case must redden.
4. Flatten a reader refusal into a single local code, dropping `sourceCode`/`sourceLayer`. The BODY_UNAVAILABLE test must redden on the source fields.
5. Move the capability check after the reader call. The capability case must redden on "reader not invoked", proving the ordering assertion is real rather than incidental.
If a drill survives, do not rationalise it: either the assertion has detached from its subject or the mutation is equivalent. Say which, with evidence.

GATE. Run exactly:
`pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck; A=$?; pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test; B=$?; echo "TC=$A TEST=$B"`
Exit codes captured separately — no pipes (a piped run reports the pipe tail's code) and no `&&` chaining (a red typecheck then hides the count line). READ THE OUTPUT: the test leg must print a `Test Files N passed` count line with a NONZERO count; `pnpm --filter` prints "No projects matched the filters" and exits 0 when a package does not resolve, so exit 0 with no count line is UNVERIFIED. @moe/daemon resolves to apps/daemon. Compare both counts against the pre-change baseline — equal or higher; a DROP means a file stopped being collected, which reads as a pass while covering less.
DoD 5 ALSO REQUIRES A PLAIN-NODE BRIDGE CHECK, which no vitest run performs: vitest rewrites `./foo.js` back to `foo.ts` and resolves through its own aliasing, so a missing or malformed `.js` bridge is invisible to the suite. Load the new bridge in a REAL child process (`node --input-type=module -e 'await import("<path>/graph-query.js")'`) and require exit 0. Record the command.
Re-measure `wc -l` on http-listener.ts (304 before) and the new module, and record both — the cap is per FILE.
Then attribute any red by the path-attributed baseline: repo-wide failures at the merge-base, again at HEAD, delta intersected with owned paths EMPTY. Report foreign red verbatim with exact failing paths; never hide it and never fabricate green.

ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW, then complete. Load the `adversarial-self-review` skill and read the diff as an attacker:
- Is `graphContentHash` ever assigned from `snapshotIdentity`, or vice versa, on ANY path including the JSON round trip? Trace both fields from the reader's output to the decoded bytes. This is the decision dec-64b2391c constraint and the reason the task rail names it.
- Can any request field influence WHICH project or WHICH revision is read? Trace `projectId` to `principal.projectId` and confirm the `boundProjectId` cross-check has no bypass.
- Does either transport re-implement any part of the authenticate/compatibility sequence rather than calling the shared handler?
- Is any reader refusal restamped or flattened? All four fields must survive.
- Did anything write? The port declares one reader and no commit; confirm no path reaches the store directly.
- Confirm every touched production file is under the per-file cap, the new bridge is an exact one-line LF file, and `git status --porcelain` shows only owned paths.
COMPLETION MUST RECORD:
1. CONSUMER: task-efc2ef6330074b4d9893809f7425c95f (wire graph commands and current-graph query) is the named consumer and final hardening task; give it the exact edge `answerGraphQuery(...)` from apps/daemon/src/planning/graph-query.js plus the two transport call sites.
2. That decision dec-64b2391c is satisfied structurally: the reader already produces `graphContentHash` and `snapshotIdentity` as separate fields, and this handler carries both through unequated — name the drill that proves it.
3. The capability constant you chose for graph.get and why.
4. THE OPEN QUESTION architect-2cc07e26 raised and I am NOT resolving: `graph.preview` sits beside `graph.get` on the same frozen vocabulary line (:76) and is equally unserved. It is outside this task's stated scope, so it stays unserved — flag it for a governor decision rather than silently widening scope.
Commit by EXPLICIT PATHSPEC only — `git commit -- <path> ...` — never a bare `git commit`, per this epic's rail 3: the index is shared state and a bare commit captures another task's staged files. Verify with `git show --stat` that only owned paths landed.

comments.content:
STALE BLOCK PREMISE — re-measured, both halves of this task's OWN stated unblock test now pass. architect-77071474, 2026-08-18, HEAD a42ae2f. Posting evidence rather than flipping status; the transition is a governor/human call.

The premise says: "Unblock test is a grep: dd4ffa0c must export a current-active reader and packages/core a real GraphRevisionContent contract." Running exactly that:

**(1) The reader EXISTS.** `task-dd4ffa0c` is now **DONE** — the premise recorded it as "BLOCKED with 0 plan steps". Its reader landed at `apps/daemon/src/planning/active-graph-projection.ts` (commit d60a48f, itself a restore after a foreign whole-tree commit captured a QA mutation drill).

**(2) `GraphRevisionContent` EXISTS.** The premise recorded `git grep "GraphRevisionContent" HEAD -- packages/ apps/` returning ZERO. It now returns five files, including `packages/scheduler/src/graph-content-fields.ts` plus the daemon's active-graph-projection and graph-body-record.

**(3) THE DECOY THIS PREMISE SPECIFICALLY WARNED ABOUT IS GONE — the part worth reading.** The premise cautioned that "@moe/scheduler already exports a symbol NAMED graphContentHash that is structural only (index.ts:86, :93); returning it as content provenance would violate the DoD while typechecking cleanly." That hazard was repaired by the very landing this task was waiting for. `graph-content-fields.ts`'s header states it directly:

> "Before decision `dec-64b2391c` the package published a `graphContentHash` computed over the graph's STRUCTURE alone — one of the seven fields — under a name that claims authority over all of them. A durable revision bound to that value would carry an identity omitting the repository base tree, parent revision, policy revision, decomposition budget and author, and would satisfy @moe/core's `validHex64` gate while doing it. **The structural value now has a structural name (`snapshotIdentity`) and this module owns the only thing entitled to be called content.**"

So `task-e3d5fd05` ("Canonical GraphRevisionContent contract, codec and content-hash producer") is **DONE**, and the sharpened DoD 2 reading — full content provenance AND a separately named structural identity, unequated — is now satisfiable rather than a trap.

**ONE NUANCE, not a blocker, but decide it deliberately:** the premise expected the contract in `packages/core`; it landed in `packages/scheduler`. `git grep -c GraphRevisionContent HEAD -- packages/core/` returns **zero**. That is a location difference, not an absence — e3d5fd05's own title calls it the canonical contract and its owner shipped it there. Whoever plans this should confirm the daemon can reach it from the `@moe/scheduler` public root by compiled probe, NOT by grep: that barrel is curated, `graphContentDigest` is deliberately internal, and `encodeGraphContent` is documented as "the only route to a hash".

**BRANCH STATUS, from this task's own premise:** "e3d5fd05 + 77e8cb44 -> dd4ffa0c -> c4b80778. Does NOT wait on 32c1ba45 or eacea969." e3d5fd05 DONE, dd4ffa0c DONE, 77e8cb44 ARCHIVED. The decision precondition (dec-64b2391c, human chose OPTION A on 2026-08-17, msg-6a6d3590) was already recorded as met. Nothing in the chain is outstanding.

Recommend promotion to PLANNING. Unblocking this also clears one of the four premises holding `efc2ef63`.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:

planningNotes.risks:
1) THE EQUATION IS THE FAILURE THIS TASK EXISTS TO PREVENT. `graphContentHash` and `snapshotIdentity` are both lowercase hex strings of the same shape, so cross-assigning them typechecks, passes a name-based grep, and satisfies @moe/core's `validHex64` gate. Only a value-level assertion against the reader's OWN output catches it — and only if the seeded revision has two genuinely different values. Verify the fixture actually differs before trusting the test.

2) A JSON ROUND TRIP IS THE OTHER PLACE THEY COULD COLLAPSE. Assert both fields survive `dispatchQueryBytes` as distinct values, not just that the call succeeded.

3) REFUSED-BEFORE-READ IS NOT VISIBLE IN A RETURN VALUE. A handler that reads another project's graph and then refuses looks identical to one that refused first. Count reader invocations with a decorator for the auth/capability/spoofing cases.

4) FOUR REFUSAL FIELDS, NOT ONE. Flattening `sourceCode`/`sourceLayer` makes a missing body indistinguishable from a corrupt one, and merges the core replay vocabulary the reader deliberately keeps separate. Assert the quadruple.

5) THE MCP QUERY PATH HAS NO CREDENTIAL TODAY. Adding the optional context is contract-compatible but easy to get subtly wrong: resolve exactly as the command path does (`context?.credential ?? config.fallbackCredential ?? null`) or stdio loses its single-process identity.

6) http-listener.ts IS 304 LINES against a 400 hard split. Measure after adding the route; extracting the read routes is the sanctioned fix, not compressing comments.

7) BRIDGES ARE INVISIBLE TO VITEST. It rewrites `./foo.js` to `foo.ts`, so a missing or malformed `.js` bridge passes the whole suite and fails under plain Node — which DoD 5 requires. Load it in a real child process.

8) SHARED INDEX. This epic's rail 3 is stricter than the others: explicit pathspec commits only, `git status --porcelain` before and `git show --stat` after.

9) OUT OF SCOPE BUT ADJACENT: `graph.preview` remains unserved on the same vocabulary line. Leave it, flag it.
